description:
`dev/simulation_results/permanent-zero-fraction/README.md` states that "an
execution receipt that identifies a manifest quotes the same value" as the
sidecar's `manifest.json` SHA-256 entry. The only manifest digest the execution
machinery actually produces is `blake3::hash` over a fresh
`serde_json::to_vec(manifest)` re-serialization
(`crates/gf2-sim/src/permanent_campaign/driver.rs:206`, consumed by
`campaign_config_hash` at `driver.rs:190-199`). An auditor comparing a field
checkpoint's recorded hash against `checksums.sha256` finds two unrelated
values with no way to tell which artifact is wrong.

Pre-existing before the campaign freeze; surfaced by the independent freeze
audit (finding 5). Either the driver's receipt identity must become SHA-256
over the on-disk manifest bytes, or the README must describe the blake3
re-serialization identity and its relation to the sidecar value. The choice
must land before the first campaign arm executes, because field checkpoints
written during draws are permanent evidence.

## Success criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The digest algorithm and byte source of the execution
  receipt's manifest identity match between the campaign README's prose and
  the driver's emitted value, verified by a test or transcribed run.
- [hard] REQ-02: An auditor's comparison path from a field checkpoint to the
  frozen manifest identity is stated in the README and actually reproduces.
title: Campaign README promises execution receipts quote the sidecar manifest SHA-256, but the driver emits blake3 over a re-serialization
